To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) it is possible to find a representative shape for a set of observations but that the shape varies with application and frequency, (2) the representative shape is not necessarily the one with the smallest air fraction and (3) the representative shape has a larger air fraction than the SPA.

(1) the soft particle approximation does not work for ice hydrometeor mass retrievals, (2) the Geer and Baordos (2014) shape model is a good approximation of mean optical particles, (3) this shape model has the desired properties also for radar and higher frequencies, and (4) the assumption on particle shapes is likely less critical if using mass equivalent diameter compared to maximum dimension.

the shape of the ice particles is the main source of uncertainty for the retrieval of ice mass from passive and active microwave observations, and that a better understanding of particle shape is therefore a key to improving the retrieval of ice hydmeteor mass.
